items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1959-03-18
items.q: And Sam Ducre taught him to use his lip on both upper and lower.

ctx.x: No, I don't believe, because any man that do that in the long run, you'd see a gutter from their teeth, it wears down into the top of the mouthpiece.

Ralph here is taking lessons from Professor Mineta, and he advises him to do that too. He says some of the old timers that used to, I think he said George Bakay too, had his teeth all worn from, it wears not only the mouthpiece but the teeth. He said he used to go around and look at the clarinet fires, and quite a few of them would have their teeth worn down too there in the middle, and he didn't do that. And Sam Ducre taught him to use his lip on both upper and lower.
Well that's one thing I could take Waltz as a one for, he liked me. He taught me that.
